title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 1 diabetes and recent hypoglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a known patient with type 1 diabetes mellitus who presents today for a routine follow-up. The patient reports experiencing a recent hypoglycemic episode while at work. They describe feeling shaky and lightheaded, which resolved after consuming a fast-acting carbohydrate. The patient has been on long-term insulin therapy and denies the use of any oral medications. They report consistent adherence to their current regimen but noted some fluctuations in blood glucose levels over the past week.

Medication List
Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. They are alert and oriented x3. Skin is clear and intact. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hypoglycemia.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. We discussed monitoring blood glucose more frequently during periods of high activity. The patient will keep a log of glucose readings and any further hypoglycemic episodes to review at the next visit. Follow up in four weeks.
explanations: Type 1 diabetes with hypoglycemia without coma: E10.649.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
